finding.title: No session revocation anywhere: 24h stateless JWT survives logout, password change, MFA disable and admin-side unbind; middleware never re-validates the user
finding.evidence: auth.go:152-155 logout() only writes an audit row; auth.go:181 password change does not invalidate tokens; auth.go:278-279 and users.go:48-49 clear the MFA secret without touching sessions; jwt.go:21 ExpiresAt 24h; Claims (jwt.go:11-15) carry only UserID/Username/RegisteredClaims; no jti/revok/blacklist/token_version anywhere in backend/; middleware.go:23-30 only parses the JWT and sets context, no DB lookup; auditws.go:31 parses the admin JWT from c.Query("token").
finding.impact: A stolen admin JWT is a 24-hour full-admin credential that cannot be withdrawn; logout, password change, MFA disable/unbind and account lockout all leave the attacker authorized.
finding.mitigations_checked: alg confusion blocked (jwt.go:31); exp enforced by golang-jwt v5; JWT not in a cookie, no CORS middleware; frontend does call POST /auth/logout (MainLayout.tsx:184-192).
finding.recommendation: token_version in Claims bumped on logout/changePassword/mfaDisable/unbindUserMfa/unlockUser/delete and compared in AuthMiddleware after loading the user; or short-lived access tokens + server-side refresh in mfaStore; replace the /audit/ws query-string JWT with a subprotocol header or a one-time WS ticket.

verification.evidence_integrity: PASS - every quoted line was read end-to-end and is verbatim and line-exact: auth.go:152-155 (logout body is exactly recordOp + ok), auth.go:181, auth.go:278-279, users.go:48-49, jwt.go:21 (`ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour)),`), Claims struct jwt.go:11-15 (only UserID/Username/RegisteredClaims), middleware.go:23-30, auditws.go:31 (`claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, c.Query("token"))`), routes.go:118 (`api.GET("/audit/ws", s.auditWS)` - registered with no AuthMiddleware), MainLayout.tsx:184-192, auth.ts:9. The primary cited line (152) is correct, so no corrected_line change is warranted.
independent_corroboration: grep over backend/ for jti|revok|Revok|blacklist|Blacklist|token_version|TokenVersion|denylist|session_version|SessionVersion => zero hits; broader grep for session|Session|force_logout|kickout|invalidate => one hit only, an unrelated comment at backend/internal/db/db.go:55.

backend/internal/model/model.go:13-26 AdminUser has no token_version, no role and no enabled/disabled column (single privilege level), and model.go:296-303 AllModels() registers no session/denylist table: &AdminUser{}, &APIKey{}, &Provider{}, &ModelAlias{}, &AliasUpstream{}, &GuardKeyword{}, &PIIRule{}, &InjectionRule{}, &Quota{}, &RateLimitRule{}, &SystemSetting{}, &ConfigVersion{}, &ConfigLoadLog{}, &CallLog{}, &OperationLog{}, &BackupRecord{}.
backend/internal/admin/middleware.go:14-33 performs zero DB access: auth.Parse then c.Set("operator"...), c.Set("userID"...) only.
auth.go:38 `if u.IsLocked() {` is the only place IsLocked (model.go:28-30) is consulted, i.e. lockout gates login attempts exclusively.
auth.go:125 `token, err := auth.Issue(s.secret, u.ID, u.Username)` is the sole issuance site; auth.Parse has exactly two call sites (middleware.go:23, auditws.go:31) - no hidden re-validation path.

No user create/delete/disable endpoint exists: routes.go:133-135 exposes only GET /users, POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa, POST /users/:id/unlock; users.go is 65 lines total (listUsers/unbindUserMfa/unlockUser); admins are bootstrapped once at main.go:164-184.
verification.why_not_refuted: Nothing asserted is false and no mitigation elsewhere in the flow neutralises it: there is genuinely no revocation primitive of any kind, /auth/logout really is audit-only, and credential-adjacent changes really do leave previously issued bearer tokens valid. The cited lines are right, so the finding cannot be refuted on evidence.
why_not_high: No new capability: exploitation requires the attacker to already hold a valid admin JWT, and that JWT by itself already grants 100% of admin power for its remaining lifetime. The missing control only denies the defender the ability to shorten a window that another vulnerability already opened. Under the stated rubric that is precisely 'medium = defense-in-depth gap w/ real impact', not 'high = authed-but-severe or account takeover' - the takeover primitive is the theft, which is not this finding.

Every theft vector named is separately filed in the same audit batch, so rating them again here double-counts severity: authn-1/critical (default JWT_SECRET makes tokens forgeable), frontend-1/medium (no CSP -> localStorage 'llm-router-guard.auth.v1' exfil on any XSS), frontend-2/medium (JWT as ?token= on /audit/ws leaking to proxy logs), frontend-4/low (credentials committed in deploy scripts).

The XSS theft vector is hypothetical, not demonstrated: grep over frontend/src for dangerouslySetInnerHTML|innerHTML|eval\(|new Function returned zero matches, so the token-theft precondition has no proven in-product path other than out-of-band log/physical exposure.

Sequencing inconsistency inside the auditor's own work: the identical WS query-string vector is used here to justify high but is scored medium in frontend-2; one of the two calibrations must be wrong.
Bounded blast radius: expiry is enforced by golang-jwt v5 default validators, so worst case is 24h from issuance, not persistent access.

Partial mitigation the finding's mitigations_checked missed: this product's own access log never records the WS token. main.go:89 uses `engine := gin.New()` (no gin.Logger) and the bespoke access logger at main.go:109 reads `path := c.Request.URL.Path` and prints only that at main.go:116-117 - never RawURI/URL.RawQuery - so the 'access log' exposure is deployment-external (a fronting proxy configured to log full URIs), not in-product.

Partial detection mitigation also missed: every admin mutation funnels through server.go:94-97 `audit.LogOp(s.db, operatorOf(c), ... clientIP(c) ...)`, so an intruder's actions are attributable to the victim username with an IP and are visible via GET /audit/operations (routes.go:114). 'Each of those actions looks successful in the UI' overstates the defender's blindness.
factual_errors_found: Impact says incident response should stop an intrusion by 'unlock the account'; unlock (users.go:54-64) clears failed_logins/locked_until and is the opposite of a containment action - it does not revoke anything and should not be listed among controls that 'should stop an attacker'.

'even deleting/locking the account leaves the bearer authorized': locking is code-accurate (IsLocked is only checked at auth.go:38), but there is no account-delete capability in the product at all (routes.go:133-135, users.go:1-65), so 'deleting the account' is not a containment lever being defeated - it requires out-of-band surgery on the SQLite file.

'no mechanism to add revocation later without a schema change' is too strong: a denylist keyed on (uid, iat/exp) - both of which jwt.go:22 already populates via IssuedAt - needs a new table but no change to AdminUser, and Claims already embeds jwt.RegisteredClaims whose ID (jti) field simply goes unset at issuance.

The finding omits the one revocation lever that does exist: Server.secret is fixed at construction (server.go:30,38 `secret: jwtSecret`) and never reloaded (configstatus.go:42-50 reloadConfig only bumps the runtime manager), so restarting with a rotated JWT_SECRET invalidates every outstanding admin token at once - blunt and global, but a real kill switch.
verification.residual_impact_at_medium: The genuinely reportable core is the interaction between lockout and statelessness: the project implements an account-lockout control for REQ-022 (auth.go:113-122, model.go:28-30) that has zero effect on an already-issued token, and the auth layer (middleware.go:14-33) never loads the user row, so the only server-side containment available to an operator is a global JWT_SECRET rotation plus restart of every instance (README requires the secret to be identical across instances). Combined with a logout that is a pure no-op (auth.go:152-155) and password/MFA changes that do not invalidate sessions (auth.go:181, auth.go:278-279, users.go:48-49), the session lifecycle is undefended - a real impact, but an amplifier of token theft rather than a standalone high-severity issue.

reason: Verdict downgrade (high -> medium), not refuted. Evidence integrity is perfect: all eight quoted locations were read end-to-end and match verbatim at the exact lines cited (auth.go:152-155 logout writes only an audit row; auth.go:181 password change; auth.go:278-279 and users.go:48-49 clear the MFA secret; jwt.go:21 24h expiry; Claims at jwt.go:11-15 carries no ID/jti beyond the unset RegisteredClaims.ID; middleware.go:23-30 parses the JWT with no DB lookup; auditws.go:31 parses the admin JWT from the query string on a route registered at routes.go:118 without AuthMiddleware). I independently corroborated the absence of any revocation mechanism: greps for jti/revok/blacklist/denylist/token_version/session_version over backend/ return nothing, model.go:13-26 AdminUser has no token_version/role/enabled column, model.go:296-303 registers no session table, auth.Issue has one call site (auth.go:125) and auth.Parse exactly two (middleware.go:23, auditws.go:31), so there is no hidden re-validation path. The finding is therefore technically true and would be confirmed if severity were the question. It is over-scored because it grants the attacker nothing they do not already hold: the JWT itself is the full-admin credential, and this finding only removes the defender's ability to shorten an exposure window that some other vulnerability opened - which is the definition of a defense-in-depth gap with real impact (medium) rather than 'authed-but-severe / account takeover' (high). Every theft vector asserted is separately filed in the same batch (authn-1 critical for the forgeable default JWT_SECRET, frontend-1 medium for the missing CSP over the localStorage token, frontend-2 medium for the very same /audit/ws query-string JWT, frontend-4 low for committed deploy credentials), so rating this high re-charges the same compromise twice, and it is internally inconsistent for the same author to score the WS query-string vector medium in frontend-2 but a high-escalating vector here. The XSS premise is also hypothetical - grep for dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/eval/new Function in frontend/src returns zero matches - and the log-leakage premise is weaker than stated because this product never logs the query string at all (main.go:89 uses gin.New() with no gin.Logger, and the access logger at main.go:109,116-117 prints c.Request.URL.Path, not RawURI/RawQuery), leaving only external proxy configuration. Two further mitigations the auditor did not weigh: exp is enforced by golang-jwt v5 so the window is bounded at 24h; Server.secret is fixed at construction (server.go:30,38) and unaffected by reloadConfig (configstatus.go:42-50), so rotating JWT_SECRET and restarting is a genuine (blunt, global) kill switch; and every admin mutation is attributable via server.go:94-97 audit.LogOp with operator and IP, readable at GET /audit/operations, so an intruder's activity is visible even though it is not stoppable. The write-up also contains real inaccuracies that argue against 'high' as filed: 'unlock the account' is not a containment action (users.go:54-64 clears the lockout), there is no delete/disable-user capability anywhere (routes.go:133-135; users.go is 65 lines; admins are bootstrapped once at main.go:164-184) so 'deleting the account' is not an in-product lever being defeated, and 'no mechanism to add revocation later without a schema change' is false since a (uid, iat) denylist needs no change to AdminUser and IssuedAt is already populated (jwt.go:22). What survives is still worth fixing and is why this is medium rather than low: the project ships a lockout control (auth.go:113-122, model.go:28-30) that is consulted only at login (auth.go:38) and therefore does nothing to an active session, and neither logout, password change nor MFA disable/unbind touches sessions, so the session lifecycle is entirely undefended apart from a global secret rotation plus restart. Recommend keeping the finding with the token-theft vectors stripped out (they belong to authn-1 / frontend-1 / frontend-2), the 'delete/unlock' framing corrected, severity medium, and the recommendation retained as written - token_version in Claims compared in AuthMiddleware after a user-row load, shorter expiry, and a one-time WS ticket instead of the long-lived JWT in the query string.
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: the attacker already possesses a valid admin JWT - obtained via a separately-reported weakness (authn-1: default/committed JWT_SECRET lets anyone forge one; frontend-2: a fronting proxy that logs full URIs captures `GET /api/admin/v1/audit/ws?token=<JWT>` as emitted by frontend/src/hooks/useAuditStream.ts:65; frontend-1: a future XSS reads localStorage['llm-router-guard.auth.v1']). No vulnerability in this finding is needed to obtain the token; this finding is what happens afterwards.

1) Attacker replays the captured bearer token indefinitely:
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/providers
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" -X PUT http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/apikeys/1 -d '{...}'
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/audit/ws?token=<jwt>   (live call-log stream; auditws.go:31 authenticates from the query string alone)
2) Defender performs the documented containment actions, each returning {"code":0}:
   POST /api/admin/v1/auth/logout  -> auth.go:152-155 only calls s.recordOp then s.ok; nothing server-side changes. The client clears localStorage (MainLayout.tsx:184-192), so the UI shows 'logged out' while the attacker's token is untouched.
   PUT /api/admin/v1/auth/password -> auth.go:181 writes password_hash only; jwt.go has no claim derived from the hash, so old tokens still pass middleware.go:23.
   POST /api/admin/v1/account/mfa/disable -> auth.go:278-279 zeroes mfa_secret/mfa_enabled; middleware never reads the user, so the token still authenticates.
   POST /api/admin/v1/users/:id/unlock -> users.go:61-62 only resets failed_logins/locked_until.
3) Even the product's own lockout does not help the defender: after 5 bad passwords auth.go:117-120 sets locked_until and auth.go:38 refuses new logins, yet the already-stolen token keeps returning 200 on all ~85 AuthMiddleware routes because middleware.go:15-32 never issues a DB read - so an operator can see 'account locked' in the UI while the intrusion continues.
4) Termination only occurs at exp (+24h from jwt.go:21) or by out-of-band global rotation of JWT_SECRET and a restart of every instance (secret fixed at server.go:30,38; reloadConfig at configstatus.go:42-50 does not touch it), which also logs every legitimate admin out and requires deployment access.

Net: attacker-visible impact is persistence-through-IR for up to 24h, contingent on the theft already having succeeded - hence medium (defense-in-depth / lifecycle gap), not high.
